s: A cross-functional team has been told by a senior manager to take on a new request every few days, outside the backlog. The team is losing focus. What is the BEST response from the project manager?
o: Let the team absorb each request and extend the sprint goal to fit the new work as it arrives
Show the manager the cost of interruptions and agree one intake route via the product owner
Assign one team member to handle all of the manager's requests outside the normal backlog
Ask the product owner to quietly drop lower-priority items whenever a new request appears
e: Protect the team by routing requests through the product owner and showing the cost of interruptions. Absorbing or side-channelling requests keeps the disruption hidden.

s: A team member and the product owner disagree about whether a story is done. The team's definition of done is clear and the story meets it. What should happen?
o: Let the product owner reopen the story until all of their added expectations are satisfied
Ask the sponsor to rule on whether the story counts as done for this particular iteration
Have the team lead decide and record the outcome as a precedent for later disputes
Hold to the agreed definition; extras become a new story or team-agreed change
e: Agreed definitions resolve disputes. New expectations become backlog items or a team-agreed change to the definition.

s: A newly formed team has strong individual performers who work in silos. Which action BEST builds team performance?
o: Tie bonuses to individual output targets
Add detailed role descriptions for each specialist
Set shared team goals and pair people across skills
Rotate the team leader each week to spread ownership
e: Interdependence and shared goals build team performance.

s: Which tool BEST shows how stakeholders' current engagement compares with the level you need?
o: Power/interest grid plotted by stakeholder
Stakeholder engagement assessment matrix
RACI chart of project responsibilities
Salience model of power and urgency
e: The engagement assessment matrix compares current and desired engagement. The power/interest grid only prioritises stakeholders.

s: A remote team member says they only learn of decisions through hallway conversations at the head office. What is the BEST fix?
o: Have the head office team brief remote members by phone after meetings
Email remote members a monthly digest of decisions made at the office
Invite remote members to hallway-style chats by scheduling optional calls
Record decisions in a shared place and announce them on one channel
e: Good communication gives equal access to information regardless of location.

s: You find that a report you issued last month contained a calculation error that makes progress look better than it was. The sponsor has not noticed. What do you do?
o: Correct it, tell the sponsor promptly what changed, and fix the check
Correct it quietly in next report and note the revision only if asked
Tell the sponsor only after confirming whether it affects any decision
Ask the report author to reissue it without drawing attention to the change
e: Honesty and responsibility: disclose and correct promptly.

s: The team lead you appointed is technically strong but intimidates others, so people hide problems. What is the BEST step?
o: Reassign the lead's tasks to others while keeping their title
Raise it at the next retrospective naming the lead's behaviour
Wait for a formal complaint before acting on the behaviour
Give private feedback with examples and coach a safer style
e: Coach first. Psychological safety is critical to surface problems early.

s: Lessons from earlier phases are not being used by new team members. What would MOST improve knowledge sharing?
o: Write a longer end-of-project lessons report for all staff to read
Searchable repository plus short briefings for each new joiner
Name one team historian to answer questions from new members
Run annual training covering lessons from all past projects
e: Knowledge must be accessible and reinforced at the point of use.

s: A stakeholder expects a monthly report but the plan has it quarterly. What should you do?
o: Discuss the need; if valid, update the communications plan
Send monthly reports now and tell the stakeholder later
Explain that the approved plan says quarterly and keep to it
Ask the stakeholder to read the quarterly report more closely
e: Align expectations and update the plan if the need is valid.

s: Which constraint makes the schedule MOST likely to need resource levelling?
o: A fixed end date with plenty of spare staff available
A mandatory dependency between two sequential tasks
Scarce shared specialist needed on parallel tasks
A long lead time on a purchased hardware component
e: Resource levelling resolves over-allocation of scarce resources.

s: EV is $250,000, PV is $300,000, AC is $275,000. What are the CV and SV?
Product backlog refinement shows that a requirement, once clear, is much larger than expected. What should the team do?
o: Extend the iteration length so the whole item fits in one cycle
Split it into smaller stories with the product owner
Re-estimate it at a larger point value and keep it as one item
Ask the team to work extra hours to fit it into the iteration
e: Large items are split so they can be delivered in a single iteration.

s: Before issuing a request for proposal you realise the statement of work is vague. What should you do?
o: Clarify the statement of work first so bids are comparable
Issue the RFP and clarify scope in the bidder conference
Ask the preferred seller to draft the statement of work
Switch to a time-and-materials contract to avoid defining scope
e: A clear statement of work leads to comparable bids and fewer disputes.

s: A process is within control limits but the mean has drifted toward the specification limit. What does this tell you?
o: Capable, because every point is inside the control limits
Out of control, so stop production and widen the limits
Stable but drifting toward the limit: investigate and re-centre
Acceptable, so add more inspection and keep running unchanged
e: Stable does not mean capable. Drift toward a specification limit needs action.

s: A team estimates in story points and reports velocity of 30. A stakeholder asks how many hours that equals. What is the BEST answer?
o: Say 30 points is roughly 300 hours using a ten-hour rate
Have the team log hours for a month, then convert points to hours
Explain points are relative, then forecast from velocity
Replace points with hour estimates so the stakeholder can plan
e: Velocity and points are not a time conversion. Forecast with velocity and remaining backlog; a fixed hours rate or a calibration exercise misrepresents what points measure.

s: A procured contractor lacks a skill stated in their contract. What should you do FIRST?
o: Verify the gap against the contract and talk to the vendor
Ask the vendor to replace them straight away at its own cost
Withhold payment until the contractor completes extra training
Reassign their tasks to employees and tell the vendor later
e: Check the facts against the contract and work through the vendor relationship before drastic action.

s: Which metric BEST shows whether work is being completed at a sustainable rate in a kanban system?
o: Velocity measured in story points per sprint
Cumulative hours logged by the team each week
Size of the backlog at the end of each week
Throughput, the items finished per period
e: Throughput is completed items per time period, which suits flow-based kanban. Velocity is a sprint measure and hours logged show effort, not completion.

s: A project manager must produce an integrated plan for a project with predictive hardware and an agile software stream. What is the BEST approach?
o: Run each stream on its own plan and merge at final delivery
Link both streams on one timeline with integration points
Convert hardware work into sprints to use one method
Freeze hardware scope and let agile adapt without sync points
e: Tailor planning to each approach and join them at integration points.

s: A project has a $50,000 contingency reserve and a $40,000 management reserve. An unplanned event costs $30,000 and was not in the risk register. What is the BEST action?
o: Use the contingency reserve and update the register after
Draw management reserve directly without needing sign-off
Offset the cost by trimming quality testing from the plan
Request management reserve through the governance process
e: Unidentified risks (unknown unknowns) draw on management reserve, which needs approval. Contingency is for identified risks in the register.

s: Final deliverables are accepted. What should you do before releasing the team?
o: Release the team now and complete the archive afterwards
Start planning the next project and finish records in parallel
Run lessons learned, archive records and complete the handover
Release the team, then run lessons learned remotely by survey
e: Closure requires lessons learned, archiving and transition before resources are released.

s: A feature's cost has doubled. How do you decide whether to proceed?
o: Continue, because the money already spent is too large to waste
Compare remaining cost to remaining value with the sponsor
Cancel the feature, since cost has doubled from the estimate
Put the feature on hold until the budget can be increased again
e: Sunk cost is irrelevant. Compare the remaining cost with the remaining value.

s: A sponsor leaves the organisation mid-project and no replacement is named. What should you do?
o: Raise it with governance so a new sponsor is named quickly
Pause all work until a replacement is named by the organisation
Carry on and make the sponsor's decisions yourself for now
Ask the project's top stakeholder to act as sponsor informally
e: Projects need an accountable sponsor. Escalate to governance promptly.

s: A vendor requires access to personal data not covered by your data agreement. What should you do?
o: Grant access under a verbal promise to sign the agreement later
Provide masked sample data for the vendor and skip the agreement
Check the agreement with legal and update it before access
Refuse access and replace the vendor with a new supplier
e: Compliance and agreements come before access.

s: Several small approved changes together now threaten the schedule. What is the BEST action?
o: Keep approving changes one by one and monitor the schedule
Absorb the effect using schedule float and report at closure
Freeze all new change requests until the end of the project
Assess combined impact and re-baseline via change control
e: Cumulative change needs a combined view and re-baselining via governance and a report to the sponsor. Approving one by one hides the total effect.

s: An issue has been open for three weeks with no owner. What should you do?
o: Move it to the risk register and review it monthly
Assign an owner and a date, escalate if needed
Wait for the owner to emerge at the next status meeting
Close it as stale because three weeks passed unchanged
e: Issues need owners and dates, with escalation where authority is lacking.

s: A residual risk remains after a mitigation. What should you do?
o: Add further mitigations until the risk falls to zero
Remove it from the register since the response was applied
Assess it, decide if it is acceptable, and monitor it
Convert it to an issue and assign it to the team lead
e: Residual risk remains after a response and should be accepted knowingly and monitored.

s: A lessons learned review shows that the same estimating error recurs across projects. What is the BEST way to improve?
o: Brief each new team on the error at its kickoff meeting
Update estimating guidance and templates using the data
Require a senior estimator to review every estimate
Send all estimators on a refresher course next quarter
e: Feed lessons into organisational process assets so the improvement lasts. Warnings, reviews and courses depend on individuals remembering.

s: A new law will take effect in four months and affects a deliverable due in six. What is the BEST action?
o: Assess the impact now and update the plan and risk register
Wait for the law to take effect, then adjust the deliverable
Ask the customer to confirm scope without analysing impact
Deliver as planned and treat any penalty as a later issue
e: Anticipate known external changes: assess impact, update the plan and risks, and take any changes through governance early.

s: The sponsor wants the project to meet an internal sustainability target not in the original requirements. What do you do?
o: Add it to the backlog at top priority without assessment
Decline it because it was not in the original requirements
Fold it into existing tasks and update the plan later
Assess the impact and process it as a change request
e: New expectations are assessed and handled through change control.
